document.title: Written Statement for the Record of the DCI
document.authors: CIA / Director of Central Intelligence (Joint Inquiry Committee)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: Written statement of the DCI before the Joint Inquiry Committee. Source: Chapter 4, Endnote 103; Chapter 6, Endnote 54; Chapter 8, Endnote 60.

persons.name: Usama Bin Ladin
persons.role: al-Qa'ida leader; early terrorist financier of Arab fighters in the Afghan war; resident in Sudan 1991-1996; relocated to Afghanistan in 1996 under Taliban sanctuary
organizations: World Islamic Front for Jihad Against Jews and Crusaders
persons.status_detail: Status in 2002 not stated in this chunk

mentions.quote: Bin Ladin gained prominence during the Afghan war for his role in financing the recruitment, transportation, and training of Arab nationals
In August 1996, Bin Ladin issued a religious edict or fatwa entitled "Declaration of War,"
In return, Bin Ladin invested vast amounts of money in Taliban projects and provided hundreds of well-trained fighters
I told key leaders at CIA and across the Intelligence Community that we should consider ourselves "at war" with Usama Bin Ladin.
Our intent was to drive up Bin Ladin's security concerns and lead his organization to delay or cancel its attacks.
we were convinced Bin Ladin meant to attack Americans, meant to kill large numbers
They worked tirelessly for years to combat bin Ladin and al-Qa'ida

persons.name: Aideed
persons.role: Somali warlord opposing US forces in Somalia in 1993; reportedly advised by Bin Ladin's members

mentions.quote: Bin Ladin sent members to Somalia in 1993 to work as advisors with Somali warlord Aideed in opposing US forces

persons.name: James Woolsey
persons.role: Director of Central Intelligence (1993); warned of terrorist WMD threat in House testimony

persons.name: John Deutch
persons.role: Director of Central Intelligence (1996); warned of terrorist use of WMD

mentions.quote: In February 1996, in testimony to the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, DCI Deutch expressed his concern

persons.name: George Tenet
persons.role: Director of Central Intelligence, author of the statement; declared CIA 'at war' with Bin Ladin in 1998
persons.status_detail: Delivered statement 17 Oct 2002 (identified by office; name not in text)

mentions.quote: In 1998, I told key leaders at CIA and across the Intelligence Community that we should consider ourselves "at war" with Usama Bin La.din.

persons.name: Khalid al-Mihdhar
persons.role: al-Qa'ida operative, later 9/11 hijacker; traveled to Kuala Lumpur January 2000

mentions.quote: We learned that his full name is Khalid bin Muhammad bin 'Abdallah al-Mihdhar.
On 4 July 2001, he returned to the US, entering in New York.
Khalid had been at a suspected al-Qa'ida logistics facility in Yemen.
Al-Mihdhar departed the US on 10 June 2000 and obtained a new passport and US visa

persons.name: Nawaf al-Hazmi
persons.role: al-Qa'ida operative, later 9/11 hijacker; traveled to Kuala Lumpur January 2000

mentions.quote: We learned in March 2000 that al-Hazmi flew from that country to Los Angeles on January 15, 2000
al-Hazmi flew from that country to Los Angeles on January 15, 2000

persons.name: Saeed Muhammad Bin Yousaf
persons.role: Key planner of the October 2000 USS Cole bombing; attended Kuala Lumpur meeting

mentions.quote: identified as Saeed Muhammad Bin Yousaf (aka Khallad), who became a key planner in the October 2000 USS Cole bombing.
On 8 January 2000, they traveled to another Southeast Asian country with Khallad.

persons.name: Ahmad Sajuli Abdul Rahman
persons.role: Malaysian logistics unit member of Jemaah Islamiah; escorted al-Qa'ida visitors in Kuala Lumpur

mentions.quote: Sajuli took the al-Qa'ida visitors around Kuala Lumpur.
Sajuli took the al-Qa'ida visitors around Kuala Lumpur. Two years later, Sajuli has been arrested

mentions.quote: Yazid Sufaat, a Malaysian chemist who... was directed by a terrorist leader to make his apartment available to the al-Qa'ida operatives.

persons.name: Zacarias Moussaoui
persons.role: Terrorist suspect later connected to Sufaat

mentions.quote: Sufaat's name would later be connected to that of Zacarias Moussaoui.
Zacarias Moussaoui was arrested but refused to provide information on the plot.

events.description: Bin Ladin resides in Sudan, combining business with jihad under al-Qa'ida.
Extremists bomb a hotel housing US servicemen in Aden, Yemen, claiming Bin Ladin financed their group.
Al-Qa'ida finances travel of over 300 Afghan war veterans to Sudan after Pakistani crackdown.
Bin Ladin sends members to Somalia to advise Aideed against US forces.
Al-Qa'ida has begun financing at least three terrorist training camps in northern Sudan.
US Embassy and CIA station in Khartoum closed.
Khobar Towers bombing in Saudi Arabia.
Bin Ladin describes Khobar Towers killings as the beginning of a war with the US.
Bin Ladin issues 'Declaration of War' fatwa.
Bin Ladin relocates from Sudan to Afghanistan.
Al-Qa'ida, as the World Islamic Front, issues a fatwa calling for killing Americans and their allies.
actors: World Islamic Front for Jihad Against Jews and Crusaders

events.description: East Africa US Embassy bombings.
USS Cole attack.
CTC's new operational strategy 'The Plan' previewed to senior CIA management.
September 11 attacks that killed nearly three thousand people.
Cruise missile attack on al-Qa'ida training camp complex in northeastern Afghanistan
DCI declares CIA 'at war' with Usama Bin Ladin
New CTC operational strategy ('The Plan') previewed to senior CIA management
CIA, FBI, State receive intelligence on suspected al-Qa'ida operatives traveling to Kuala Lumpur
Surveillance began with arrival of Khalid al-Mihdhar in Kuala Lumpur; ended 8 January
Al-Mihdhar, al-Hazmi and Khallad travel to another Southeast Asian country
Al-Hazmi and al-Mihdhar enter US via Los Angeles
Al-Mihdhar departs the US
USS Cole bombed; 17 US sailors killed
Al-Mihdhar re-enters US at New York
CIA sends immediate message requesting watchlisting of al-Mihdhar and al-Hazmi
Kuala Lumpur meeting of al-Qa'ida operatives (6-8 January) including Khallad, al-Mihdhar and al-Hazmi, hosted by Sajuli and Sufaat's apartment.
Al-Mihdhar and al-Hazmi traveled to another Southeast Asian country with Khallad.
Al-Hazmi (and al-Mihdhar) entered the US at Los Angeles.
Al-Mihdhar departed the US.
USS Cole bombing, in which Khallad was a key planner.
Al-Mihdhar re-entered the US via New York.
CIA sent immediate message to State, INS, Customs and FBI requesting al-Mihdhar and al-Hazmi be watchlisted.
DCI open-session testimony warning of Bin Ladin attacks.
DCI 'declared war' against al-Qa'ida after East Africa embassy bombings.
First attack on the World Trade Center; a plot against New York City tunnels and landmarks was broken up.
Bombing of US embassies in Africa; in fall 1998 the DCI asked for more than $2.0 billion annually in additional intelligence funding.
Millennium plot to attack Los Angeles airport foiled when a young terrorist panicked at the Canada-US border.
CIA had the equivalent of 700 officers working counterterrorism.
September 11 attacks.
Attempted shoe bombing on an airliner stopped by crew and passengers.
CIA Counterterrorist Center created to fuse intelligence sources.
Bin Ladin Issue Station opened; FBI officers detailed soon after.
After East Africa bombings, FBI and CIA disrupted planned attack on another US Embassy in Africa; over 20 al-Qa'ida operatives arrested in three days.
CIA reported plot to hijack a plane on the US east coast to free the Blind Shaykh.
CIA Inspector General report found CIA-FBI interactions too personality dependent.
CIA with Middle Eastern partner arrested two Bin Ladin operatives planning attacks on US facilities in Saudi Arabia.
CIA launched wide-ranging disruption effort against Bin Ladin's organization in June and July 2001.
Middle East partner detained a terrorist directed to attack US Embassy or cultural center in a European capital.
Local authorities arrested an operative described as Bin Ladin's man in East Asia, acting on CIA information.
CIA, FBI and State received intelligence on suspected al-Qa'ida operatives traveling to Kuala Lumpur; CIA initiated surveillance operation.
US multiple-entry visa issued to al-Mihdhar in Jeddah (expiring 6 April 2000).
CIA obtained photocopy of al-Mihdhar's passport as he traveled to Kuala Lumpur but did not watchlist him; passed copy to FBI.
Al-Mihdhar arrived in Kuala Lumpur and surveillance began; ended 8 January when he left.
Al-Mihdhar left Kuala Lumpur; surveillance ended.
CIA begins receiving reports Bin Ladin plans to move from Sudan.
US Embassy and CIA station in Khartoum closed for security reasons.
Khobar Towers bombing in Saudi Arabia, later described by Bin Ladin as start of a war.
Bin Ladin describes the Khobar Towers killings as the beginning of a war between Muslims and the US.
Bin Ladin issues 'Declaration of War' fatwa authorizing attacks on Western military targets on the Arabian Peninsula.
Bin Ladin interview explaining the need for qualitative operations and good preparation.
Al-Qa'ida under the World Islamic Front banner issues fatwa calling for killing Americans and allies.
actors: World Islamic Front for Jihad Against Jews and Crusaders

events.description: Attack on the USS Cole.
Bin Ladin interview calls acquisition of WMD a religious duty.
DCI Woolsey testifies to House Foreign Affairs Committee on WMD terrorism risk.
DCI Deutch testifies to Senate Select Committee on Intelligence on WMD terrorism.
CIA publishes two assessments on al-Qa'ida CBRN capabilities.
FY2000 budget submission describes Bin Ladin as most significant sponsor of Sunni extremist terrorism.
US cruise missile attack against the al-Qa'ida training camp complex in northeastern Afghanistan.
Military campaign began to topple the Taliban and destroy al-Qa'ida.
CIA Counterterrorist Center created.
Millennium threat period: integrated CIA-FBI campaign to disrupt al-Qa'ida; 36 additional terrorist agents identified, operations in 50 countries, 21 disrupted.
USS Cole bombed; 17 American sailors killed.
Ramadan period peak threat; terrorist cells in the Persian Gulf region broken up, explosives and anti-aircraft missiles captured.
After East Africa bombings, more than 20 al-Qa'ida operatives arrested in three days in an African country to disrupt a planned attack on another US Embassy.
Reports of plot to hijack a plane on the US east coast to free the Blind Shaykh; CIA/FBI advisories issued.
A plot was uncovered in Manila in early 1995; the conspirators studied regional security procedures when choosing method and venue.
The White House Commission on Aviation Safety and Security reported on the changing terrorist threat.
actors: White House Commission on Aviation Safety and Security

events.description: A National Intelligence Estimate said civil aviation remained a particularly attractive terrorist target.
DCI Tenet 'declared war' against al-Qa'ida after the East Africa embassy bombings.
In early 1999 the Intelligence Community surged more than 800 analysts to support the NATO bombing campaign against Yugoslavia.
After the African embassy bombings, in fall 1998, Tenet asked the Administration for over $2.0 billion more in annual intelligence funding for FY2000-2005.
Bin Ladin relocated to Afghanistan.
Tenet told CIA and IC leaders the US should consider itself 'at war' with Bin Ladin.
Tenet ordered a baseline review of CIA operational strategy; CTC produced 'The Plan' in spring 1999.
Pakistani nuclear tests strained US-Pakistan relations.
Military coup in Pakistan strained US relations.
Cruise missile attack on an al-Qa'ida training camp complex in northeastern Afghanistan.
Bombing of a hotel housing US servicemen in Aden, Yemen by Islamic extremists who said Bin Ladin financed them.
Bin Ladin sent members to Somalia to advise Aideed against US forces.
Al-Qa'ida financed travel of 300+ Afghan war veterans to Sudan after Pakistani crackdown.
Al-Qa'ida had begun financing at least three terrorist training camps in northern Sudan.
Bin Ladin described the Khobar Towers killings as the beginning of a war between Muslims and the US.
Bin Ladin issued fatwa 'Declaration of War' authorizing attacks on Western military targets on the Arabian Peninsula.
Bin Ladin interview explaining why no attacks followed the August fatwa.
Al-Qa'ida under World Islamic Front banner issued fatwa to kill Americans and allies worldwide.
actors: World Islamic Front for Jihad Against Jews and Crusaders

events.description: East Africa US Embassy bombings by al-Qa'ida.
Establishment of the Bin Ladin Issue Station.
Bin Ladin left Sudan and relocated to Afghanistan.
National Intelligence Estimate warns of terrorist threats to US civil aviation, citing Manila plot.
Plot uncovered in Manila in early 1995.
National Intelligence Estimate says civil aviation remains an attractive terrorist target.
White House Commission on Aviation Safety and Security reports changing terrorist threat.
actors: White House Commission on Aviation Safety and Security

events.description: Tenet testifies in open session on Bin Ladin's planned attacks.
Tenet testifies Bin Ladin wants to strike further blows against America.
Hani Hanjur, replacement pilot for Flight 77, in the US by end of 2000.
Intelligence Community Counterterrorism Board issues threat advisories; FAA issues two alerts to air carriers.
CIA, FBI and State received intelligence on suspected al-Qa'ida operatives traveling to Kuala Lumpur; CIA initiated an operation.
US multiple-entry visa issued to al-Mihdhar in Jeddah.
CIA obtained a photocopy of al-Mihdhar's passport as he traveled to Kuala Lumpur.
Surveillance began with al-Mihdhar's arrival in Kuala Lumpur; ended 8 January when he left.
Kuala Lumpur meeting 6-8 January; Sajuli escorted al-Qa'ida visitors; Khallad attended.
Al-Mihdhar and al-Hazmi traveled with Khallad to another Southeast Asian country.
Al-Hazmi (and al-Mihdhar) flew to Los Angeles and entered the US.
USS Cole bombing, planned by Khallad.
CIA directed a file review; CTC found al-Mihdhar and al-Hazmi had entered the US.
CIA sent immediate message to State, INS, Customs and FBI to watchlist al-Mihdhar and al-Hazmi.
NSA lost all communications between headquarters and field stations, unable to process information for several days.
After the US embassy bombings in Africa, DCI asked the Administration to increase intelligence funding by more than $2.0 billion annually for FY2000-2005.
Speaker Gingrich approved a funding list topped by counterterrorism; first significant infusion of new money for US intelligence in the 1990s.
CIA had the equivalent of 700 officers working counterterrorism at headquarters and in the field.
CIA counterterrorism budget request was less than four percent of the total CIA program.
First attack on the World Trade Center; a plot around the same time to attack New York City tunnels and landmarks was broken up.
At the Millennium, a young terrorist panicked at a Canada-US border crossing and his plan to attack Los Angeles airport was exposed and thwarted.
Another young terrorist on an airliner tried to detonate explosives in his shoes and was stopped by crew and passengers ("last winter").
Speaker Gingrich approved counterterrorism at the top of the FY1999 funding list, the first year of significant new intelligence funding.

September 11 suicide terrorist attacks, referenced by the DCI as the point after which Intelligence Community effectiveness increased; the DCI states the US was vulnerable to such attacks and remains so.

key_claims: Bin Ladin financed the recruitment, transport and training of Arab fighters during the Afghan war but had no direct US government contact then.
In Sudan (1991-96) al-Qa'ida financed Afghan veteran travel and at least three training camps, and Bin Ladin's group was linked to the Aden bombing and Somalia advisers.
The Taliban sheltered Bin Ladin, assigned guards and allowed camps, in return for Bin Ladin's money and hundreds of fighters, making this 'a terrorist sponsoring a state'.
Al-Qa'ida/Taliban camps trained militants sent on to Kashmir, Chechnya and Bosnia, forming a worldwide network.
CIA's 1999 'The Plan' aimed to capture Bin Ladin and lieutenants, but was hindered by no US presence in Afghanistan, strained Taliban relations, and strained US-Pakistan relations.
CIA declared itself 'at war' with Bin Ladin in 1998 and created 'The Plan' in 1999 to capture him and his lieutenants.
US policy stopped short of replacing the Taliban, limiting pressure on Bin Ladin.
Pakistan was the principal access point to Afghanistan, but relations were strained by 1998 nuclear tests and 1999 coup.
CIA HUMINT on al-Qa'ida grew from about 600 reports in 1998 to 900 in the first nine months of 2001.
Khallad, a USS Cole planner, was the most important attendee at the January 2000 Kuala Lumpur meeting, supported by a JI logistics network.
CIA failed to watchlist al-Mihdhar and al-Hazmi despite having sufficient information in January and March 2000.
Khallad was judged the most important figure at the Kuala Lumpur meeting because of his later role in the USS Cole bombing.
The content of the Kuala Lumpur meeting remains unknown.
CIA failed to watchlist al-Mihdhar and al-Hazmi despite opportunities before August 2001.
Jemaah Islamiah, an al-Qa'ida affiliate, provided logistics support in Kuala Lumpur.
CIA warned repeatedly that Bin Ladin intended mass-casualty attacks but lacked actionable detail on the 9/11 plot.
CIA argues counterterrorism funding rose despite overall intelligence budget declines in the 1990s.
CIA counterterrorism funding rose over 50% above FY1997 levels before 9/11 despite an overall budget decline of 18% in real terms in the 1990s.
About 700 CIA officers worked counterterrorism in August 2001, excluding liaison services.
Sending forces into the terrorist sanctuary changed the rules, and al-Qa'ida must never again acquire a sanctuary.
Al-Qa'ida keeps its most lethal plots within a small, tightly knit group, making total success impossible.
